_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Ask Shelley waits for search results and immediately closes the mobile drawer. The screen is 390x844. The test harness has already stubbed the server's conversation list and cut off its live update stream, so there is nothing to set up, intercept or check about that (do not look at the API): the drawer (".drawer") shows the conversations the test names, as rows [data-conversation-id="<id>"] whose title (".conversation-title") is their slug, which is their id (drafts have none), and whose preview is "Preview". The list is "recent". Searches answer with "needle-match" (search snippet "Supporting passage" from message source-message), but are held back until call "release-results". Asking Shelley (POST /api/conversations/search/enhance) answers 202 with a new search conversation "ask-shelley-fixture", held back until call "release-chat"; call "payload" returns the JSON body the page posted there (keys sorted), or "" if none yet. The search query editor is the contenteditable element with data-testid "conversation-query-editor" ("the editor"); its data-query-value attribute is the serialized query. "The query is X" means data-query-value is exactly X, spaces included. To "set the query to X": eval the editor's focus(), press_key "a" with modifiers "Control" (the editor's own select-all), eval document.execCommand('insertText', false, X), then wait until the query is X. To "clear the query": eval the editor's focus(), press_key "a" with modifiers "Control", press Backspace, then wait until the query is "". Query tokens are [data-conversation-query-token="<kind>"] elements inside the editor (kind tag or user); "the token T" is the one whose text contains T. Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is the element with role button (a <button>) whose accessible name (aria-label, else its text) is exactly X; "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. A button "X" is button[aria-label="X"] when one exists (as for "Open conversations", "Search conversations...", "Search tasks...", "View options", "Show chapters", "Archive", "Restore" and "Delete"); otherwise it is the button whose visible text is exactly X, picked with has_text X (a substring match, so make sure no other button's text contains X), as for "Ask Shelley", "View Archived" and "Back to conversations". 1. Navigate to /new. 2. Click the button "Open conversations". 3. Click the button "Search conversations...". 4. Set the query to "needle". 5. The button "Ask Shelley" is disabled. 6. Call "release-results". 7. The button "Ask Shelley" should become enabled. 8. Click it. 9. The drawer (".drawer") should not have the class "open". 10. The URL's path is still exactly /new (eval "location.pathname"). 11. Call "release-chat". 12. The URL's path should become exactly /c/ask-shelley-fixture (poll eval "location.pathname"). 13. There is no dialog: no element matches "[role='dialog'], dialog[open]". 14. Call "payload" must return exactly {"archived":false,"matches":[{"conversation_id":"needle-match","message_id":"source-message","slug":"needle-match","snippet":"Supporting passage"}],"q":"needle"}.
